title: WavePolyp: Video Polyp Segmentation via Hierarchical Wavelet-Based Feature Aggregation and Inter-Frame Divergence Perception
claim: Target objects in adjacent frames are camouflaged and vary in position, shape and size, making consistent tracking hard.
layout: 5 panels left-to-right, each an adjacent frame pair with masks below
description: A single horizontal strip of five panels labeled (a) to (e), separated by dashed vertical lines. Each panel shows two strictly adjacent colonoscopy frames in the top row, with the matching binary ground-truth polyp masks (white blob on black) in the bottom row. Panels (a) and (b) show polyps that blend into the surrounding mucosa, so they are hard to see. Panels (c), (d) and (e) add red bounding boxes on the polyp. Between the two frames of each pair the polyp moves (c), changes shape (d) or changes size (e). The eye goes first to the reddish endoscopic images and the red boxes, then down to the masks.
caption: Challenges in VPS: (a) and (b) the high camouflage of polyps, (c) position variation, (d) shape variation, (e) size variation. Note that (a)-(e) represent two strictly adjacent frames.
abstract: Automatic polyp segmentation from colonoscopy videos is a crucial technique that assists clinicians in improving the accuracy and efficiency of diagnosis, preventing polyps from developing into cancer. However, video polyp segmentation (VPS) is a challenging task due to (1) the significant inter-frame divergence in videos, (2) the high camouflage of polyps in normal colon structures and (3) the clinical requirement of real-time performance. In this paper, we propose a novel segmentation network, WavePolyp, which consists of two innovative components: a hierarchical wavelet-based feature aggregation (HWFA) module and inter-frame divergence perception (IDP) blocks. Specifically, HWFA excavates and amplifies discriminative information from high-frequency and low-frequency features decomposed by wavelet transform, hierarchically aggregating them into refined spatial representations within each frame. This module enhances the representation capability of intra-frame spatial features, effectively addressing the high camouflage of polyps in normal colon structures. Furthermore, IDP perceives and captures inter-frame polyp divergence through a temporal divergence perception mechanism, enabling accurate polyp tracking while mitigating temporal inconsistencies caused by the significant inter-frame variations across frames. Extensive experiments conducted on the SUN-SEG and CVC-612 datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms other state-of-the-art methods. Codes are available at \url{https://github.com/FishballZhang/WavePolyp.
